frequency_question: How often does an institutional or structural block prevent a scheduled rate increase when the central bank governing body is attempting a tightening cycle?
membership_rule: Includes every scheduled FOMC meeting within recognized modern monetary policy tightening cycles (1994-1995, 1999-2000, 2004-2006, 2015-2018, 2022-2023) where the prevailing direction was upward. Excludes emergency inter-meeting moves unless explicitly part of the scheduled rate trajectory.
provenance_note: claims 40 cases from only 5 named (8.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 5 major cycles fully enumerated; zero instances of structural friction successfully halting a desired hike once the cycle of tightening was formally initiated at a scheduled meeting.
known_gaps: Intra-meeting dissent occurs, but structural vetoes preventing the chair/majority from implementing a scheduled rate decision do not exist within the FOMC voting framework.
skeleton: Five distinct federal reserve tightening cycles comprising over 40 individual rate-increase decisions where internal structural friction or external institutional vetoes failed to block the enacted hikes once initiated.
multiplier: 5 cycles * average ~8 rate increases per cycle = ~40 instances of attempted and executed tightening blocks.
validity_reason: The institutional voting structure and lack of external structural friction on FOMC rate decisions remain fixed by statutory design under the Federal Reserve Act.
